items.followUp: An element has atomic number 11. How many electrons are present in its K, L and M shells?

rubric.why: The shell distribution accounts for all 17 electrons.
rubric.description: Gives the correct numbers of electrons in all three shells.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for K = 2, L = 8 and M = 7; award 1 mark if two shells are correct.

modelAnswer: Atomic number = number of electrons in a neutral atom = 17.
K shell = 2 electrons; L shell = 8 electrons; M shell = 7 electrons.

items.followUp: What type of ion is formed when an atom gains two electrons?

rubric.why: Losing negatively charged electrons leaves the atom positively charged.
rubric.description: States that an atom becomes positively charged when it loses electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the positive charge or cation.

rubric.why: Gaining negatively charged electrons makes the atom negatively charged.
rubric.description: States that an atom becomes negatively charged when it gains electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the negative charge or anion.

modelAnswer: When an atom loses one or more electrons, it becomes positively charged and forms a cation.
When an atom gains one or more electrons, it becomes negatively charged and forms an anion.

rubric.why: Mendeleev’s law concerns the elements’ physical and chemical properties.
rubric.description: Identifies the properties as physical and chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the relevant properties.

rubric.why: The defining relation is periodicity with respect to atomic mass.
rubric.description: States that the properties are periodic functions of atomic masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the periodic relationship to atomic mass.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev’s Periodic Law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.

items.followUp: How many elements are present in the 4th and 7th periods of the modern periodic table?

rubric.why: The 5th period has 18 elements and the 6th period has 32 elements.
rubric.description: Gives the number of elements in each requested period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct period and count.

items.followUp: How does atomic size change down a group and across a period from left to right?

rubric.why: Atomic size generally decreases across a period from left to right.
rubric.description: States the trend in atomic size across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic size decreases across a period.

rubric.why: Each step down a group adds an electron shell, increasing atomic size.
rubric.description: States the trend in atomic size down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic size increases down a group.

modelAnswer: Across a period, atomic size generally decreases from left to right.
Down a group, atomic size increases.

items.followUp: What causes the path of light to become visible when it passes through a colloid?

rubric.why: The effect is caused by colloidal particles scattering light.
rubric.description: Identifies the scattering of light as the cause.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning scattering of light by colloidal particles.

rubric.why: Scattered light makes the path of the beam visible.
rubric.description: States that the light path or beam becomes visible.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the path of the light becomes visible.

modelAnswer: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, which makes the path of the light beam visible.

items.followUp: Define a double covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond involves three shared electron pairs.
rubric.description: States that three pairs of electrons are shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the three shared pairs.

rubric.why: The shared pairs form a covalent bond between atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies the bond as covalent and formed between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the shared pairs join atoms covalently.

modelAnswer: A triple covalent bond is a covalent bond in which two atoms share three pairs of electrons.

items.followUp: Why does water have a higher boiling point than methane?

rubric.why: Water molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
rubric.description: Mentions hydrogen bonding between water molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying intermolecular hydrogen bonds in water.

rubric.why: More energy is needed to overcome the strong attractions between water molecules.
rubric.description: Links stronger attractions to the greater energy needed for boiling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that more energy is required to separate the molecules.

modelAnswer: Water molecules form strong, extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
More energy is needed to overcome these attractions, so water has a higher boiling point than alcohol.
